plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes crowded with tiny violet-blue flowers. The blooms hum with bees and release a sweet, herbal perfume that drifts across sunny gardens and Mediterranean hillsides in midsummer.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to August, so mid-June falls right at the start of peak bloom
plants.location: Temperate Northern Hemisphere, including the gardens and lavender fields of southern Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The name lavender is widely thought to come from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.description: Dense, fine-leaved shrubs light up Australian winter bushland with upright, bottlebrush-like spikes of glowing orange-gold. The flowers open slowly from the base upward over several weeks. They draw honeyeaters and other nectar-feeding birds and mammals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn through winter, roughly March to August, so mid-June is in the middle of the Southern Hemisphere bloom
plants.location: Coastal heathland and sandstone country of New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: Each banksia 'flower' spike is made up of thousands of tiny individual flowers. After flowering, the spikes develop woody follicles that often stay closed until fire sweeps through, which releases the seeds.
